questions.stem: Why does aluminium appear to be less reactive than expected, even though it is high in the reactivity series?

options.text: Aluminium reacts with nitrogen in the air, forming a gas
Aluminium forms a protective oxide layer on its surface that prevents further reaction
Aluminium only reacts at temperatures above 1000°C

questions.explanation: Although aluminium is quite high in the reactivity series, it forms a tough, protective layer of aluminium oxide on its surface almost instantly. This oxide layer prevents oxygen and water from reaching the metal underneath, making aluminium appear less reactive than it actually is.
